svg.title: The client reports severe nausea and vomiting and dark, prune-juice-colored discharge. Fundal height measures larger than expected for dates. Ultrasound shows a dense cluster of vesicles with no fetus or fetal heartbeat.
svg.desc: Hyperemesis, a uterus large for dates, prune-juice-colored bleeding, and an ultrasound showing a vesicular mass with no viable fetus are classic for gestational trophoblastic disease, not placenta previa or ectopic pregnancy, neither of which shows a vesicular mass. Because hCG must be trended weekly and then monthly for up to a year to rule out choriocarcinoma, and pregnancy would also raise hCG and confound that follow-up, reliable contraception is required during that period; there is no fixed 5-year pregnancy ban, and a future pregnancy is not destined to be molar again.
